newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel chief says developing new small car.
newsitem.headline: Opel chief says developing new small car.

text.p: German carmaker Adam Opel AG said on Monday it was developing a new small car to compete against rivals Volkswagen AG and Ford Motor Co in the highly competitive market segment.

Opel Managing Director David Herman told Reuters in an interview the new car would compete against the Seat Arosa, which was unveiled last March at the Geneva car show, and against the two-door Ford Ka.
"We are seriously working on such a project," Herman said. But he added: "Their concepts are different from ours," when comparing the Opel car under development compared to the VW and Ford models.
He declined comment on when the car might be introduced into the European market.
Opel has also unveiled its new seven-seater Zafira compact van, which will be unveiled at the Frankfurt car show in September and introduced into the European market in late 1998.
The vehicle, which is 4.32 meters long and based on technical develops gleaned from the new Astra, will have a price of less than 32,000 marks ($18,400).
"We expect the Zafira to be a hot model and to redefine the compact van market in Europe," Herman said.
